name: Lomaiviti
world_status: statement found in an open source

new_statements.quote: In all languages under study except those of Lau (LAU and VBL), the penultimate stress rule is qualified by the rule that stress always falls on the first vowel of a low or mid to high vowel sequence. In Lau, however, there is no qualification to the penultimate stress rule, so it is the second vowel of such a sequence that is stressed when it occurs in penultimate position. Thus we may contrast: NWN 'raica' 'see it' / LAU 'raica'; ONO 'rauta' 'enough' / VBL 'rauta'. [p. 160-161:] ... such sequences occurring in penultimate position appear to violate the general principle of measure-penultimate stress (Schutz 1976).
new_statements.citation: Geraghty, Paul A. 1979. Topics in Fijian language history. PhD dissertation, University of Hawaii at Manoa, sec. 3.10 'Diphthongization', p. 68 (restated sec. 4.5.2, pp. 160-161).
new_statements.check: confirmed by a second reader, with minor differences
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Opened (418 pp.) and rendered PDF p. 88 (= diss. p. 68) and PDF p. 181 (= diss. p. 161) to PNG; also read lines 5712-5730, 11605-11625). Sec. 3.10 'Diphthongization' reads exactly as quoted: 'In all languages under study except those of Lau (LAU and VBL), the penultimate stress rule is qualified by the rule that stress always falls on the first vowel of a low or mid to high vowel sequence. In Lau, however, there is no qualification to the penultimate stress rule, so it is the second vowel of such a sequence that is stressed when it occurs in penultimate position. Thus we may contrast:' with examples NWN ráica / LAU raíca 'see it', ONO ráuta / VBL raúta 'enough'. The only difference…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Stress falls on the penultimate vowel/mora of the measure (Schütz's accent unit) in every Fijian communalect Geraghty sampled, including Lovoni on Ovalau (Lomaiviti); everywhere except Lau, a low or mid vowel followed by a high vowel (ai, au, ei, ou...) counts as one unit stressed on its first vowel, so rái-ca not ra-í-ca.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Not discussed for Lomaiviti; Geraghty only notes that Western communalects lengthen phrase-antepenultimate a as an intonation peak (sec. 3.9), which does not apply to Eastern varieties.
new_statements.exceptions: Lau and Vanua Balavu (Lauan, not Lomaiviti) lack the diphthong qualification; Vanua Levu communalects delete the unstressed vowel of such sequences (raca). Stress is otherwise tied to the measure, so long vowels / two-syllable measures behave as in Standard Fijian (Schütz 1985 ch. 36).
new_statements.domain_note: Word/measure level (measure-penultimate); the dissertation is a comparative-historical survey and treats stress in one paragraph, with the general statement covering all 38 communalects rather than a Lomaiviti-specific description. The only Lomaiviti-province communalect in the sample is Lovoni (Ovalau).
new_statements.identity_note: The only Lomaiviti-province communalect in Geraghty's 38-communalect sample is Lovoni (villages Lovoni, Visoto, Nacobo, Nukutocia, Ovalau Island), which Glottolog's reference records for both Geraghty 1979 and 1983 map to Lomaiviti [lmv] / loma1261, but which Geraghty himself (fn. 2, p. 74) classes linguistically with Eastern Viti Levu (closest to Namena). No data on the Gau, Koro, Nairai or Batiki varieties that make up the rest of lmv were found in any accessible source; the stress statement is a blanket one for all Fijian communalects except Lau.

In Lau, however, there is no qualification to the penultimate stress rule, so it is the second vowel of such a sequence that is stressed when it occurs in penultimate position. sources.note: Sec. 3.10 (diss. p. 68 = PDF p. 88): in all 38 communalects under study except Lau (LAU, VBL) the penultimate stress rule is qualified so that stress always falls on the first vowel of a low/mid + high vowel sequence (raica vs Lau raica); sec. 4.5.2 pp. 160-161 restates 'the general principle of measure-penultimate stress (Schutz 1976)' for Fijian. The sample includes communalect 17) Lovoni (Ovalau Island, Lomaiviti), p. 28, which Glottolog maps to lmv; Geraghty fn. 2 p. 74 classes Lovoni linguistically with Eastern Viti Levu. No Gau/Koro/Nairai/Batiki communalect in the sample.

sources.note: Lomaiviti pages: stub, islands Koro, Makogai, Levuka, Ovalau, Batiki, Nairai, Gau; ~1,600 speakers (Ethnologue 2000); nothing on phonology. Fijian page stress statement is for Standard/Boumaa Fijian, not Lomaiviti.

sources.citation: Schütz, Albert J. 1985. The Fijian Language. Honolulu: University of Hawaii Press (open-access reissue, CC BY-NC-ND 4.0, 905-page PDF).
sources.note: Standard (Bauan) Fijian only: ch. 36.1 'Measures' (p. 553) — every measure has one accented syllable, on the penultimate short syllable or on a long syllable; ch. 4.7, 41 on measure division. Lomaiviti islands appear only in quoted 19th-c. sources (Hale: dialect of Ovalau, Koro, Gau 'very nearly the same' as Rewa) and a syntax note on Moturiki ki; no Lomaiviti stress statement.
